gaps: Every tolerance, range, and stability criterion in this chapter is stated only in degrees Celsius; the chapter gives no Fahrenheit threshold at all, and the only degrees-Fahrenheit content is the conversion formula in the front matter.

States that dissolved-oxygen, conductivity, and pH determinations rely on accurate temperature but gives no correction equation, coefficient, or table for temperature-compensating any of them (no DO solubility table, no specific-conductance reference-temperature correction).

Gives no accuracy specification for air-temperature measurement distinct from water: the +/-0.05 and +/-0.2 degrees C requirements are written for water sensors and the chapter never states an air-temperature accuracy requirement.

Gives no procedure for temperature sensors used above 45 degrees C or below -5 degrees C; for the >40 degrees C case it says only that additional comparison points are required, without saying how many or at what temperatures.
Gives no sensor drift rate, expected service life, or replacement interval, and no procedure for qualifying or correcting data already collected when a sensor fails its verification.

Gives no procedure for continuous unattended monitoring: the measurement procedures are explicitly for attended discrete measurements, and continuous-monitor operation is deferred to Wagner and others (2006) without restating any requirement.
Gives no numeric sensor response time or time constant; equilibration is specified only as heuristics (at least 2 minutes in a bath, no less than 60 seconds in situ, 3-5 minutes in air).
Gives no verification guidance for saline, estuarine, or high-conductivity water, and no numeric depth limit for immersion (deferred entirely to the manufacturer).

Gives no numeric criterion for the 'one-point comparison immediately before the field trip' - it never states how closely that single point must agree with the certified sensor, unlike the +/-0.2 degrees C stated for the five-point comparison.
Contains no procedure, threshold, or definition for turbidity, ORP, or pH measurement itself; the chapter is single-parameter and treats other metrics only as consumers of temperature data.
